newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac urges more EU dialogue with China.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac urges more EU dialogue with China.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday called on the European Union (EU) to expand its political dialogue with China, the country which he said would determine the direction of the 21st century.

"Yes, the time has come for a new approach between China and the West, based on mutual recognition, regard for each other and common adherence to the great universal values," Chirac said in a speech in Shanghai as he wound up a four-day visit to China.
Some EU members, including France, have previously clashed with China over the issue of human rights.
But France last month declined to back a motion in the United Nations Human Rights Commission criticising China's human rights record, sparking protests from international groups.

"I proposed to (Chinese) President Jiang Zemin that the European Union and China should engage in far more political dialogue, because they are both attached to the emergence of a multipolar world," Chirac said.
In Beijing this week, Chirac signed an agreement with Jiang to build political and economic ties into the next century. The visit also saw the signing of $1.8 billion in deals for French firms.

The French president said in his speech that China should be brought into a new, multipolar world and he pledged support for Beijing's bid to join the World Trade Organisation, currently under negotiation with members of the body.

"For almost 20 years the extraordinary economic and social development of China has impressed the world," Chirac said. "It (China) completely changes the world equilibrium. It will determine that of the 21st century."
Chirac said France could help China develop and urged further cooperation, particularly in the aviation and energy.
The contracts signed in Beijing in Chirac's presence included a $1.5 billion accord to sell 30 Airbus passenger jets to Chinese airlines.
The main construction work on China's latest nuclear power plant at Ling'ao in southern China, for which French company Framatome is supplying the nuclear reactors, also began during the week.
Chirac said France could help China deal with the fallout from rapid economic development and pledged help in the areas of urban planning, environmental protection and social protection.
He extended an invitation to 50 young Chinese architects to complete their training in France.
Paris has also proposed the establishment of a working group on environmental law and technology, as well as exchanges to help China set up a modern public health system, Chirac said.
